diagnosis: Spanning Tree Protocol Loop / Ethernet Backhaul Broadcast Storm

conditions.description: Is your device connected to the local Wi-Fi network / Access Point?
Can your device successfully ping the local default gateway IP (e.g. 192.168.1.1)?
Are mesh access point satellites connected via wired Ethernet backhaul switches?
Are network switch port activity lights flashing continuously at extreme frequency (broadcast storm)?

explanation: An unmanaged switch without IEEE 802.1D/w STP has formed a bridging loop between wired and wireless backhauls, causing packet storm saturation.
solution:
1. Temporarily unplug the Ethernet cable from the satellite mesh nodes.
2. Enable Spanning Tree Protocol (STP/RSTP) in your managed switch configuration.
3. Verify whether your mesh system supports simultaneous wired backhaul or requires AP isolation.
author: Dr. Sarah Lin (Senior Network Architect)
review_notes: Validated: Solves frequent mesh network bridging storms reported in enterprise and home installations.

diagnosis: TCP Socket Address Already in Use (Port Collision)

conditions.description: Does your computer meet the software's minimum OS version and architecture requirements?
Do you have at least 5 GB of free storage space on your system partition?
Does an error dialog specifically mention missing DLLs?
Does application console output report 'Errno 98 / 10048: Address already in use' or port bind collision?

explanation: Another active process or orphaned daemon has already bound exclusively to the designated TCP/IP listening socket.
solution:
1. Run 'netstat -ano | findstr <port_number>' in terminal to identify the conflicting PID.
2. Terminate the blocking process via 'taskkill /PID <pid> /F' or Task Manager.
3. Alternatively, reconfigure the application port setting to an available port.
author: DevOps Engineer Alex Kumar
review_notes: Crucial addition for developer and server software runtime troubleshooting.

diagnosis: SPI Bus Clock Phase/Polarity (CPOL/CPHA Mode) Inversion

conditions.description: Is the onboard Power LED steadily illuminated?
Are SPI sensor register bytes arriving bit-shifted or inverted (e.g. 0xAA received as 0x55)?

explanation: The microcontroller SPI master is sampling data on the wrong clock edge (Mode 0 vs Mode 3 mismatch).
solution:
1. Check the sensor datasheet for SPI Mode specification (CPOL 0/1, CPHA 0/1).
2. Update SPI.beginTransaction(SPISettings(..., SPI_MODE0/1/2/3)) in firmware.
author: Embedded Systems Engineer Maria R.
review_notes: Under review for formal bus timing verification.
